title: Efficient Bayesian Inference for the Bradley--Terry Model
text: speedyBBT R package fitting Bradley-Terry models pairwise comparison data using fast, fully Bayesian MCMC. Given set pairwise judgements – two wards higher rate forced marriage, two tennis players won match, two neighbourhoods looks deprived – speedyBBT estimates quality parameter every item compared, along full posterior uncertainty. Inference carried using Pólya-Gamma data augmentation scheme, makes sampling fast even large numbers items comparisons. package supports: standard Bradley-Terry model (speedyBBTm()), optimised speed ties comparison-specific effects; ties, comparison-specific effects (e.g. home advantage), item-level covariates via formula interface (BBTm()); multivariate normal prior distributions item quality parameters, structure items (e.g. spatial adjacency) can encoded directly prior; optional hyperparameter inference prior scale. package can used data collected using Comparative Judgement Interface.

text: code chunks show use package fit Bradley–Terry model data set relating forced marriage. Judges shown pairs wards asked higher rate forced marriage. can use speedyBBTm function draw samples full conditional distributions ward quality parameters. place multivariate normal prior distribution ward quality parameters. covariance matrix prior distribution constructed using network representation wards Nottinghamshire.
code: #View Data data("forcedMarriage", package = "speedyBBT") head(forcedMarriage$comparisons) #>   user            time win lost #> 1    1 16:08:26.316839  67   31 #> 2    1 16:08:47.888894  19    9 #> 3    1 16:09:14.093517  18   74 #> 4    1 16:09:23.666987  56   68 #> 5    1 16:09:42.930976  50   66 #> 6    1 16:09:51.129570  53   15   #Construct covariance matrix expA  <- expm::expm(forcedMarriage$adjacencyMatrix) prior.var <- diag(diag(expA)^-0.5) %*% expA %*% diag(diag(expA)^-0.5)      #Fit model library(speedyBBT) forcedMarriageModel <- speedyBBTm(outcome = rep(1, length(forcedMarriage$comparisons$win)),                                   player1 = forcedMarriage$comparisons$win,                                    player2 = forcedMarriage$comparisons$lost,                                    player.prior.var = prior.var) lambda_draws  <- parameter(forcedMarriageModel, "lambda")  lambda_centered <- lambda_draws - rowMeans(lambda_draws)  #View Trace Plots plot(lambda_centered[, 10], type = 'l',      xlab = "Iteration", ylab = expression(lambda[10])) plot(lambda_centered[, 20], type = 'l',       xlab = "Iteration", ylab = expression(lambda[20])) plot(lambda_centered[, 30], type = 'l',       xlab = "Iteration", ylab = expression(lambda[30])) plot(lambda_centered[, 40], type = 'l',       xlab = "Iteration", ylab = expression(lambda[40])) plot(parameter(forcedMarriageModel, "alpha.sq"), type = 'l') #View Results forcedMarriageModelMeans <- colMeans(lambda_draws) forcedMarriageModelLowerCI <- apply(lambda_draws, 2, quantile, 0.025) forcedMarriageModelUpperCI <- apply(lambda_draws, 2, quantile, 0.975) forcedMarriageResults <- data.frame("ward" = forcedMarriage$wards$NAME,                                     "mean" = forcedMarriageModelMeans,                                     "lowerCI" = forcedMarriageModelLowerCI,                                      "upperCI" = forcedMarriageModelUpperCI) forcedMarriageResults <- forcedMarriageResults[order(forcedMarriageResults$mean), ]  plot(forcedMarriageResults$mean, xlab = "Ward", ylab = "Posterior Mean", ylim = c(-7.5, 7.5)) segments(x0 = 1:nrow(forcedMarriageResults), y0 = forcedMarriageResults$lowerCI,           y1 = forcedMarriageResults$upperCI)

code: ############################################ ## Deprivation in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania ## ## Seymour et al (2022)                   ## ############################################ # Construct covariance matrix based on spatial informartion prior.var <- expm::expm(darEsSalaam$adjacencyMatrix) prior.var <- diag(diag(prior.var)^-0.5) %*% prior.var %*% diag(diag(prior.var)^-0.5)   # Fit BT model with ties # Using `n.iter = 3` here to reduce model runtime, you will need # a larger number of iterations for valid inference. darTiedModel <- BBTm.ties(   n.objects = nrow(darEsSalaam$adjacencyMatrix),   outcome = darEsSalaam$comparisons$outcome,   player1 = darEsSalaam$comparisons$subward1,   player2 = darEsSalaam$comparisons$subward2,   player.prior.var = prior.var,   hyperparameter = TRUE,   rw.sd = 0.005, n.iter = 3, burn.in = 0, verbose = FALSE )  # Get posterior means darTiedModelLambda <- parameter(darTiedModel, "lambda") -   colMeans(parameter(darTiedModel, "lambda")) lambda.mean <- rowMeans(darTiedModelLambda)  # Generate trace plots plot(lambda.mean)  plot(parameter(darTiedModel, "theta"), type = "l")
